headline: Harriman's facility master plan presented; no school option adopted, and a public hearing is set for October 28, 2026.
summary: Harriman presented a facility master plan covering aging infrastructure, about $197 million in 10-year repair needs, and a 10.6% K-12 enrollment decline. Options A through F were discussed, and no option was adopted. Members requested more analysis before deciding, and a public hearing is set for October 28, 2026 at 6:00 pm.

SPECIAL BOARD OF EDUCATION 
WEDNESDAY, OCTOBER 21, 2026 
NHS NORTH BOARD ROOM 
 
A special meeting of the Board of Education was held at NHS North on Wednesday, October 21, 2026.  Ms. Bishop 
called the meeting to order at 6:06 pm. 
 
Present: Ms. Giglio, Ms. Prinn (7:15 pm), Mr. Johnson, Ms. Raymond, Ms. Lewis, Mr. Salvi, Ms. Lamphier, Ms. 
Lopez, and Ms. Bishop 
 
Also Present: Dr. Andrade, Dr. Scarpati, Mr. O’Rourke, Lisa Sawin (Harriman)  
 
The purpose of this Special BOE meeting is the presentation of the Facility Master Plan by Harriman. 
 
Opening and purpose 
• Ms. Bishop called the Special Board of Education meeting to order and framed the goal as evaluating the 
facilities recommendations using district needs and available information. 
• Ms. Lisa Sawin of Harriman introduced the presentation agenda: findings, changes in education, project 
purpose and approach, options, phasing, and next steps. 
• The project assesses facilities and options; it does not determine funding sources, tax impacts, or 
educational implementation. 
Assessment findings 
• Harriman reported aging infrastructure, approximately $197 million in 10-year repair needs, and 
approximately $114 million in program-space modifications. 
• A $2 million annual CIP allocation would cover about $20 million of identified repairs over 10 years.  
• Enrollment projections show a 10.6% K–12 decline through 2034–35; elementary schools were reported at 
about 78% utilization. 
• Board members questioned capacity assumptions, birth-rate data, security upgrades, program costs, and 
comparisons with nearby districts. 
Educational visioning 
• Workshops and community input identified priorities including safety, accessibility, flexible learning 
spaces, STEM/STEAM, collaboration, technology, and outdoor learning.  
• Members discussed ensuring equitable investment and support for general education and special education 
students. 
Options and feedback 
• Options A–F ranged from keeping all 12 elementary schools open to consolidations, new schools, and a 
staged approach. Option E proposed closing five schools and was considered infeasible.  
• Community feedback included opposition to closing neighborhood schools, transportation and equity 
concerns, and requests for transparency and long-term phasing. 
Phasing and next steps 
• Harriman illustrated a possible staged path from Option F toward Options C or D, with review points and 
potential implementation over about 10 years; no option was adopted. 
• A public hearing is set for Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 6:00 pm. Members requested additional 
analysis and information before deciding. 
Open questions 
• What phased plan and school configuration should the district pursue, and how will the city fund the 
required work? 
• What are the elementary utilization assumptions, low-end program-cost estimates, neighboring-district 
comparisons, and detailed staffing and transportation effects of possible closures?  
• How should the district weigh the savings from a closure against community impacts, unused- property 
costs, and educational consequences? 
 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Lopez, to adjourn at 8:47 pm.  So voted. 
 
Submitted by Tara C. Kinsella
